record.paper_title: Some Open Problems in Topological Algebra
record.original_question: Is there a metrizable o-bounded topological group G such that player I has a winning strategy in the game OF(G)? Here a subset A of a topological group G is o-bounded if for every sequence (U_n) of neighborhoods of the origin there exists a sequence of finite sets (F_n) such that A is contained in the union of F_n U_n, and in the game OF(A), player I chooses neighborhoods U_n while player II chooses finite sets F_n, with player II winning when A is contained in the union of F_n U_n.

evidence.quote:
A subset A of a topological group G is called o-bounded if for any sequence (Un)n∈ω of neighborhoods of the origin of G there is a sequence (Fn)n∈ω of finite subsets of G such that A ⊂ S n∈ω FnUn. ... Next, given a subset A of a topological group G, consider the following game OF(A) (abbreviated from Open-Finite). Two players, I and II, choose at every step k ∈ ω a neighborhood Un ⊂ G of the origin, and a finite subset Fn of G, respectively. At the end of the game, the player II is declared the winner if A ⊂ S n∈ω FnUn. ...
Problem 11 (Banakh). Is there a (metrizable) o-bounded topological group G such that the player I has a winning strategy in the game OF(G)?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $G$ be a topological group with identity (origin) $e$. A subset $A \subseteq G$ is called o-bounded if for every sequence $(U_n)_{n\in\omega}$ of neighborhoods of $e$ in $G$ there exists a sequence $(F_n)_{n\in\omega}$ of finite subsets of $G$ such that
$$A \subseteq \bigcup_{n\in\omega} F_n U_n.$$
Given a subset $A \subseteq G$, define the two-player game $\mathrm{OF}(A)$ (Open–Finite) as follows. At each step $n \in \omega$, player I chooses a neighborhood $U_n \subseteq G$ of $e$, and then player II chooses a finite subset $F_n \subseteq G$. Player II wins the play if $A \subseteq \bigcup_{n\in\omega} F_n U_n$; otherwise player I wins.

Question: Does there exist a metrizable o-bounded topological group $G$ such that player I has a winning strategy in the game $\mathrm{OF}(G)$?
artifact.category_tag: o-bounded topological groups and selection games
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is posed by Banakh in a list of open problems in topological algebra. Related work (Banakh, "On index of total boundedness of (strictly) o-bounded groups", 2002) shows under Martin's Axiom the existence of OF-undetermined o-bounded subgroups in non-locally compact Polish abelian divisible groups, but does not resolve whether player I can have a winning strategy in OF(G) for a metrizable o-bounded group G. No published resolution of this specific question was found.

status_evidence.title: On index of total boundedness of (strictly) o-bounded groups
status_evidence.snippet: Under (MA) every non-locally compact Polish Abelian divisible group contains a Baire o-bounded OF-undetermined subgroup.
status_evidence.claim: Related results on OF-determinacy in o-bounded groups, but do not answer whether player I can have a winning strategy in OF(G) for a metrizable o-bounded group G.
